technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Implement multi-binder configuration support following Spring Cloud Stream conventions, allowing multiple connection factories per binding type and a routing/selection strategy to choose which external system to read from or write to.

U2: Modify the HDFS resource loader to detect HA namenode configuration and switch from NameNodeProxies.createNonHAProxy to NameNodeProxies.createHAProxy with appropriate HA configuration (nameservices, namenode RPC addresses).

U3 & U4: Port modules following Spring Cloud Stream binder/processor conventions. Repackage as standalone Spring Cloud Stream sink/processor modules with updated Maven/Gradle coordinates and dependency declarations.

U5 & U6: Add new REST endpoints to the existing XD/Spring Cloud Data Flow job management controller, returning JSON representations. Use the existing job deployment/composition metadata to derive the flag and graph.
U7 & U8: Modify the existing admin UI (Angular-based) to add visual styling differences for composed vs. single jobs and implement navigation routing that handles both cases.
Implement all features in a single increment using existing frameworks, build tools, and test infrastructure.
No major refactoring of the core Spring framework; only the modules/extensions noted in the user stories are affected.
assumptions: The development environment (JDK 17+, IDE, build system like Gradle/Maven) and project repositories are already set up and accessible.
The Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, and related project codebases referenced in the user stories are available and buildable.
Testing frameworks (JUnit, Spring Test, Mockito) and CI infrastructure are already configured.
A single mid-to-senior level developer with full-stack Java/Spring and frontend experience performs all activities.
For U1, the 'binding type' refers to Spring Cloud Stream binders; multiple external systems means multiple binder configurations per binding type with explicit selection per channel.
For U3 and U4, the source XD modules have stable, well-documented APIs that can be ported without major rewrites.
For U5-U8, the existing job composition data model already exists and only needs to be exposed via REST and UI.
The user stories are independent enough to be developed in parallel or sequentially without significant interdependencies.
No new infrastructure provisioning (servers, databases) is required.
Documentation updates are limited to inline Javadoc and minimal README/release notes updates.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Multi-connection support for same binding type
activities.activity_description: Design and implement support for connecting to multiple external systems for the same binding type. Extend configuration model to declare multiple target systems, update binder/connection factory abstractions, add routing/selection logic for read and write channels, and write unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: U2 - HDFS HA namenode support for custom module location
activities.activity_description: Modify the HDFS module location resolver to detect HA namenode configuration and use NameNodeProxies.createHAProxy instead of createNonHAProxy. Update related Hadoop configuration classes, add tests for HA scenarios, and verify the issue from spring-xd-ambari#14 is resolved.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Cassandra module migration from XD to Spring Cloud Stream
activities.activity_description: Analyze the existing XD cassandra module, refactor it as a Spring Cloud Stream sink, update dependencies, packaging, and configuration metadata, port the tests, and verify it works as a streaming pipeline sink.

activities.activity_name: U4 - analytic-pmml module port from XD to Spring Cloud Stream
activities.activity_description: Analyze the existing XD analytic-pmml module, refactor it as a Spring Cloud Stream processor for PMML-based scoring, update dependencies, packaging, and configuration metadata, port the tests, and verify it works as a streaming pipeline processor.

activities.activity_name: U5 - REST endpoint for job composition flag
activities.activity_description: Add a new REST endpoint to the job management controller that returns the job composition flag (indicating parent-child relationship vs. standalone). Implement the service-layer logic to derive the flag from the existing job deployment model, and add controller and unit tests.

activities.activity_name: U6 - REST endpoint for job composition graph
activities.activity_description: Add a new REST endpoint that returns the job composition graph data structure (nodes and edges) suitable for building a visual representation of parent-child job relationships. Design the JSON schema, implement service-layer graph traversal logic, and add controller and unit tests.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Visual differentiation between composed and single jobs
activities.activity_description: Update the admin UI to visually distinguish between job-composition workflows and single jobs. Add icons, colors, or labels, consume the new job composition flag endpoint, and verify the UI renders correctly for both cases.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Navigation to job detail page
activities.activity_description: Update the admin UI so that clicking on a job (whether singular or part of a composed job) navigates to the correct detail page. Adjust routing and click handlers to handle both cases consistently.
